newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat says Israel not ready to work for peace.
newsitem.headline: Arafat says Israel not ready to work for peace.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Thursday said Israel was not ready to work to save Middle East peacemaking.

"How can you dance the tango alone? You need a partner who is ready to dance with you. We say, 'Is this government really ready to work with us to preserve the peace process and protect it, is it really ready to do so?' I am sorry to say the answer is no," Arafat said in the West Bank town of Ramallah.

Arafat, speaking to a group of Israeli peace activists and left-wing legislators, slammed sanctions Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government had imposed against Palestinians since a July 30 double suicide bombing of an Israeli market.

"Netanyahu has to understand that patience has limits...If we have starvation or spoilage of goods what will happen? A disaster...Instead of fighting terrorism he is fighting the Palestnian people," Arafat said.
He made his comments a day after U.S. envoy Dennis Ross ended a mission to restore Israeli-Palestinian security cooperation after the bombing which killed 16 people, including the attackers.

Israel insists it will not lift a closure of the West Bank and Gaza Strip or make financial transfers it owes the Palestinians until Arafat cracks down on militants. Arafat says he has fought militants.
